author: Opus subagent writing as designers
status: Provisional model-authored judgments; not independent expert ground truth.

policies.goals_policy: Expected goals reflect communication outcomes requested in the brief, not every taxonomy goal associated with an expected technique.
policies.subjects_policy: subjects lists required useful subject words; not_subjects lists particular instruction, format, or mechanism words that should not become subject searches. Other sensible subject words are not penalized by these lists.
policies.techniques_policy: Expected techniques require a named mechanism or concrete descriptive evidence. A mood or generic style alone does not establish a mechanism. Explicitly negated techniques are excluded.

cases.text: Looking for chiaroscuro portraits for a jazz festival poster. Moody, intimate.
cases.rationale: Chiaroscuro is named directly; moody and intimate are mood words, not a requested communication outcome.

cases.text: Frame within a frame shots for a hotel brochure - rooms seen past a pulled-back curtain, or a courtyard glimpsed through an open door.
cases.rationale: The mechanism is named and reinforced by curtain and door openings enclosing the subject.

cases.text: Leading lines, something like a long pier running out to sea. It's for an annual report cover and I want people's eye pulled to the very end of it.
cases.rationale: Named technique with an explicit request to pull the eye along to a point.

cases.text: Show me visual puns, like a lightbulb that's also something else, for an innovation campaign.
cases.rationale: Visual pun names the metaphor mechanism, and the campaign asks to express the abstract idea of innovation.

cases.text: Atmospheric perspective references - hills fading back in layers - for a wellness app onboarding screen.
cases.rationale: Atmospheric perspective is named and the hills are described as separate receding planes; wellness context implies no stated outcome.

cases.text: I need a good odd-one-out image for a slide about standing out from competitors. Rows of the same thing, one that's different.
cases.rationale: Odd one out is named with rows of identical items setting the pattern; the slide asks for one thing to stand out, with no concrete subject given.

cases.text: Figure-ground illusion for a logo moodboard, the two faces making a vase kind of thing.
cases.rationale: The reversible-figure mechanism is named and illustrated by the classic face/vase example.

cases.text: Shallow depth of field shots of perfume bottles, the hero bottle needs to pop.
cases.rationale: Shallow depth of field is named and the brief asks for one bottle to stand out.

cases.text: A tiny hiker on the edge of a massive glacier, for a climate report cover.
cases.rationale: A small familiar figure set against a huge form makes the glacier's size legible.

cases.text: Poster for a dance night. I want it to feel like everyone's caught off the ground mid-jump, hair flying, total energy.
cases.rationale: Bodies caught mid-action with hair flying are concrete motion cues, and energy is the stated outcome.

cases.text: Hero image for a meditation retreat site: one small canoe on a big flat lake with nothing else around, top half left clear for the headline. Should feel still.
cases.rationale: An isolated small subject in an empty surround with space reserved for type is negative space; stillness is the requested outcome.

cases.text: Shots looking straight up at skyscrapers so they feel like they're closing in on you. Book cover about the city.
cases.rationale: An extreme upward viewpoint is described, and the closing-in feeling is a request for unease.

cases.text: Packaging moodboard for a coffee brand - burlap sack next to a glossy ceramic cup, rough versus slick.
cases.rationale: Coarse and glossy surfaces set side by side describe texture contrast without naming it.

cases.text: Someone standing in an open garage door with the sunny street behind, so you only see their outline in black.
cases.rationale: A dark featureless figure against bright light is a silhouette, and the door opening encloses the figure.

cases.text: Editorial spread on loneliness in cities: one guy on a bench, the crowd flowing past together, and he's clearly off on his own.
cases.rationale: Separation by distance from a group carries the meaning, and the spread asks to show the idea of loneliness.

cases.text: Interiors where the whole room is shades of one sage green, walls, sofa, everything. For a paint brand.
cases.rationale: A single hue in many tones across the whole image is a limited-palette harmony.

cases.text: Website hero, a road running dead straight through a forest and vanishing at the horizon. Product name sits right where it ends.
cases.rationale: A converging road carries the eye to a deliberate end point where the name will sit.

cases.text: A woman glancing toward the edge of the frame so the text column beside her feels connected to her.
cases.rationale: The figure's look is used to direct attention toward the adjacent text.

cases.text: For a festival poster I want everything off-kilter, like the world is tipping over - buildings and horizon cocked hard on purpose.
cases.rationale: Deliberately tipped buildings and horizon put the main lines on a diagonal, asking for instability.

cases.text: Just the hands of an old fisherman mending a net, no face, filling the whole picture.
cases.rationale: A part standing for the whole and filling the frame is a tight crop.

cases.text: Pitch deck slide on the past meeting the future: a horse-drawn cart parked next to an electric car.
cases.rationale: Two unlike things placed together for comparison express the abstract old-versus-new idea.

cases.text: A giraffe standing in an office lift, completely deadpan. Ad campaign about thinking differently.
cases.rationale: An animal in a setting where it does not belong is incongruity, used to carry the campaign's idea.

cases.text: Mountain ridges stacking back one after another, each paler and bluer than the last. Book jacket, calm tone.
cases.rationale: Overlapping planes that fade paler and bluer with distance combine layering and aerial perspective; calm is requested.

cases.text: One red umbrella in a sea of black ones, shot from high up. Annual report, theme is individuality.
cases.rationale: A single colour exception in a repeated field, seen from above, is used to express individuality.

cases.text: A face lit from one side by a single desk lamp, rest of the room pitch black. Thriller novel cover.
cases.rationale: One directional light against deep darkness is tonal contrast, and the thriller cover asks for tension.

cases.text: Looking down on a market square where the stall roofs make a neat grid of colour.
cases.rationale: An overhead view turning repeated roofs into a regular grid gives viewpoint plus pattern.

cases.text: Older couples dancing in little twos spread across a big hall. Leaflet for a community centre, it's about connection.
cases.rationale: Pairs clustered with gaps between them read as units, and the leaflet asks to show who belongs together.

cases.text: Lanterns lined up along a jetty, getting smaller as they go out into the dusk. Wedding invite, should feel peaceful.
cases.rationale: A diminishing series of lanterns along a receding jetty gives rhythm and a line into depth; peaceful is requested.

cases.text: Cathedral nave shot dead centre, left and right sides matching each other, for an order-of-service booklet.
cases.rationale: A central axis with matching halves describes symmetry without naming it.

cases.text: Bright orange kayak on a dark teal river for a sporty brand's homepage. It has to jump out.
cases.rationale: A warm accent against a cool field is colour contrast, used to make the kayak stand out.

cases.text: Single tree on a wide, empty hillside for a pension brochure. Calm, but please not a black outline against a sunset.
cases.rationale: An isolated subject in empty surroundings is negative space; the silhouette treatment is explicitly refused.

cases.text: Team photo ideas for an About page, people clustered naturally in little groups. Avoid the stiff symmetrical line-up look.
cases.rationale: Clustering into groups is described while symmetry is explicitly ruled out.

cases.text: Product shot of a wristwatch, not too busy, lots of plain surface around it. And no blurry bokeh stuff, I want it sharp front to back.
cases.rationale: Quiet plain surroundings isolate the watch; selective focus is explicitly excluded.

cases.text: Menu cover: a big bowl of noodles dead centre, both halves balanced, calm. Avoid anything tilted or shot from weird angles.
cases.rationale: A centred subject with balanced halves is symmetry; diagonal energy and unusual vantage points are refused.

cases.text: Conference banner, city at night. Not hazy or foggy - crisp right to the horizon, with buildings overlapping deep into the distance.
cases.rationale: Overlapping buildings receding into space build depth by layering, while haze-based atmospheric perspective is excluded.

cases.text: Something nostalgic for a bakery's Instagram, warm and homely.
cases.rationale: Only mood and subject are given; no visual mechanism or outcome is described.

cases.text: Pictures of beekeepers for a honey label.
cases.rationale: A plain subject request with no mechanism or communication goal.

cases.text: Moody ocean pictures for a podcast cover about grief.
cases.rationale: Mood and topic only; moodiness does not establish any mechanism.

cases.text: Hopeful, optimistic shots of kids planting trees for an NGO annual report.
cases.rationale: Emotional tone and subject only, with no compositional or visual mechanism described.

cases.text: Old harbour towns, any time of day, for a travel zine spread.
cases.rationale: A subject-only request; no mechanism or outcome is asked for.
